abort.no_devices_found: No IOTBT / LEDnetWF devices found nearby. Make sure the lights are powered and not connected to the phone app.

init.title: Dazzle Bright
init.description: Pick how this device is controlled. String lights (e.g. IOTBTCC3) use pattern templates; segment bars (e.g. IOTBT4E8) get a night-light switch and a signal-colour select.

data.blank_off: Turn off by blanking the LEDs (no white flash)

data_description.power_on_first: Off (recommended): a pattern turns the lights on by itself, like the vendor app does. Turn on only if your lights stay dark when a pattern is sent while they are off; this brings back a brief flash.
data_description.blank_off: On (recommended): 'off' sets every LED to black and leaves the controller running, so turning on goes straight to the pattern. Off: 'off' really powers the string down, and the lights flash white on the next power-on.

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description:
One template per line: `name: arguments`, using dazzle_multicolor.py arguments (e.g. `christmas: random red green blue purple`, `meteor: anim meteor --speed 70 red white`). Brightness comes from the light; `static` uses the LED count below unless it has its own `--points`.

{error}

data.point_count: Number of LEDs on the string

data_description.input_select: When this helper changes, the template with the same name is applied. An option can also carry its own command: `name: arguments`.

segments.title: Segment bar
segments.description:
The layout gives one entry per segment, top to bottom; `name*N` repeats an entry. `night` shows the night colour while the Night light switch is on (black when off), `signal` shows the colour picked in the Signal select, and anything else is a fixed colour name or RRGGBB. Use exactly as many entries as the bar has segments (18 on the IOTBT4E8): with more, the lights squeeze and blend them.

{error}

data_description.night_color: A colour name or RRGGBB, e.g. ff8811.
data_description.signal_colors: Comma-separated options for the Signal select. Each is a colour, or label=colour to send a different colour under a friendly name, e.g. black, red, yellow=ff4400, green, blue, purple.

error.invalid_template: Invalid template - see the message above.
error.invalid_segments: Invalid setting - see the message above.

send_command.name: Send command
send_command.description: Send any dazzle_multicolor.py command line to the lights. Brightness is taken from the light.

command.name: Command
command.description: For example: anim fallingSnow --direction 2 white blue
